notes:
Instruction sets ACC8 and RV32I, wide program memory and its editor

The coming CPU chapters need programs longer than 16 bytes and
processors with real instruction sets. Instruction sets are now a
registry: ACC8 (the 8-bit accumulator CPU, 16-bit words) and RISC-V
RV32I, each with an assembler with labels (RISC-V with the usual pseudo
instructions), the meaning of every word and an emulator the levels
take their expected outputs from. The new wide program memory holds up
to 4096 words of up to 32 bits; its editor shows the program text,
each line's words and meaning, the instructions and a test run - as
hex words until a level unlocks the assembler. Program tests read a
wide output lamp and the text on displays.
